To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lifelong learning for older adults in museums, archives and in the context of street art is a way to develop older adults' capabilities for active ageing.
lifelong learning for older adults is a way to develop their civic and health capabilities through engagements in Nordic museum, archives and street arts.
lifelong learning for older adults is a prerequisite for their active ageing and that this is a prerequisite for the health and well-being of older adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a framework that can be used by cultural heritage institutions to develop activities for older adults in the context of lifelong learning for active aging.

the question of whether and how cultural heritage institutions can provide opportunities for older adults to develop capabilities in relation to lifelong learning for active aging in museums and archives and street art.
how older adults can be supported to develop diverse civic and health capabilities through lifelong learning for active aging in museums and archives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lifelong learning for older adults in cultural heritage institutions contributes to the development of civic and health capabilities, which in turn contributes to active ageing.
lifelong learning for older adults in museums, archives and in street art activities can help to develop older adults' capabilities to live a good and meaningful life in their later years.
lifelong learning in Nordic museums and archives for active ageing is an important part of the development of civic and health capabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lifelong learning for older adults is not only an educational activity but also a social and cultural process in which older adults' develop civic capabilities that are necessary for their health.
lifelong learning in cultural heritage institutions is a way of developing older adults' health and civic capabilities, and thereby a way of contributing to active ageing.
older people need to develop diverse civic capabilities in relation to the educational life course in order to be able to develop their health capabilities in the context of active ageing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
older adults need to be able to develop a range of capabilities to be able to engage in lifelong learning for active aging.

lifelong learning for older adults' needs to be seen not as a way to develop a set of skills, but rather as a process that develops older adults' capabilities to live a good life, which is a process that is never finished.

older adults need to be seen as active learners who can contribute with their own knowledge, experience and skills to the development of their own health capabilities in the context of lifelong learning activities in cultural heritage institutions.
